title: Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Leads 3 Day 40-Km Padyatra Titled ‘Hyderabad Walks For Nasha Mukt Bharat’, Culminating In Grand Finale At Jubilee Hills in Hyderabad, Telangana
subtitle:
Walk Organised As Part Of The 100-Week ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva For Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’ Launched By Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi
Three-Day Padyatra From Amberpet To Jubilee Hills Receives Overwhelming Public Participation, Bringing Together Youth, Public Representatives, Padma Awardees, Film Personalities, Sportspersons, Spiritual Leaders And Citizens
Three Padma Vibhushan Awardees – Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, Dr. K. Chiranjeevi And Dr. D. Nageshwar Reddy Grace The Concluding Ceremony
body_text: The three-day Padyatra titled ‘Hyderabad Walks for Nasha Mukt Bharat’ , led by Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy, concluded with a grand finale at Jubilee Hills, in Hyderabad, Telangana on Friday. Covering approximately 40 kilometres across the city from November 25 to 27, the Padyatra witnessed overwhelming public participation and emerged as a significant citizen-led mobilization against drug abuse, carrying the message of a drug-free India to communities, educational institutions and public spaces across Hyderabad. The initiative was organized in furtherance of the 100-week ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’ , launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in August this year, and in support of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) of the Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Photo 1: Beginning the day with yoga before the yatra Photo 2: Hon’ble MP Dr. K. Laxman, former Governor Shri Bandaru Dattatreya, former MLC Shri N. Ramchander Rao and renowned actor Shri Daggubati Venkatesh take the Nasha Mukt Bharat pledge The event sought to mobilize young people, families, educational institutions and civil society organisations to collectively address the challenge of substance abuse and strengthen the national resolve towards a Nasha Mukt Bharat. Describing the Padyatra as a people's movement that transcends political affiliations, Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy reiterated the Government's commitment to making India drug-free by 2029. He called upon young people, parents, educational institutions and citizens to actively participate in the campaign and make the fight against substance abuse a sustained social movement. While announcing the initiative, Shri G. Kishan Reddy had emphasised, “No father should see his son’s future getting destroyed because of drugs,” underlining that protecting children and young people from substance abuse is a shared responsibility of families, communities and society at large. Photo 3: Citizens, students and volunteers march with the Tricolour - Say No to Drugs’ banner Photo 4: Students, NSS volunteers and citizens walk with the Tricolour Calling for building together a Nasha Mukt Bharat , Shri Reddy urged people to come forward and extend helping hand for the p ersons seeking assistance for de-addiction, as well as their family members. He said anyone can access counselling and referral services through the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment's 24×7 National Toll-Free Drug De-addiction Helpline 14446 . Photo 5: Hon’ble MPs Shri Eatala Rajender and Shri Konda Vishweshwar Reddy, Hon’ble MLA Shri Alleti Maheshwar Reddy, Hon’ble MLCs Dr. Chinnamail Anji Reddy and Shri Malka Komaraiah, along with actors Kumari Payal Rajput and Shri Nikhil Siddhartha, join the walk at Osmania University Photo 6: Spiritual Leaders and Community members join the walk Beginning at Amberpet on November 25, the Padyatra traversed several prominent locations and landmarks of Hyderabad, including Osmania University Arts College, the Ambedkar Statue at Tank Bund, Balkampet Yellamma Temple and Maitrivanam at Ameerpet, before culminating at Jubilee Hills. Floral tributes were also paid to Bharat Ratna Dr. B.R. Ambedkar during the walk. Photo 7: Floral tribute to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar during the walk Photo 8: Students and youth take the Nasha Mukt Bharat pledge along the route The Padyatra was marked by enthusiastic participation from students, NSS volunteers, youth groups, residents, civil society organisations, sportspersons, film personalities, doctors, healthcare and IT professionals, educationists, spiritual and community leaders, artists and voluntary organisations. The participants began the day with yoga and subsequently set out carrying the Tricolour, wearing campaign T-shirts and caps, and displaying banners bearing messages such as ‘Say No to Drugs’ and ‘Don’t Let Drugs Dictate Your Life’. Photo 9: Renowned actor Shri Bellamkonda Sai Sreenivas and badminton legend and Chief National Coach of the Indian National Badminton Team Shri Pullela Gopichand join the walk Photo 10: Film director Shri Boyapati Srinu, actor Shri Sai Kumar and mimicry artist Shri Siva Reddy join the walk At universities, public gatherings and programmes organised along the route, participants and citizens took pledges to stay away from drugs and support individuals and families affected by substance dependence. Photo 11: Spiritual leaders and dignitaries on stage along with Shri Vijay Anand Reddy Photo 12: Nagarjuna Akkineni extends his support to the walk The extensive participation reflected the growing recognition that prevention of substance abuse requires sustained community engagement and collective responsibility. The concluding ceremony at Jubilee Hills was graced by three Padma Vibhushan awardees namely Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, spiritual leader and Founder of the Art of Living; Dr. K. Chiranjeevi, renowned film personality and former Union Minister; and Dr. D. Nageshwar Reddy, noted gastroenterologist and Chairman of AIG Hospitals. Addressing the gathering, Dr. K. Chiranjeevi appealed to young people to remain away from drugs and intoxicants, describing substance abuse as a serious menace capable of derailing their aspirations, ambitions and future. He urged the youth to recognize their responsibilities towards their families and the nation and contribute actively to building a healthy and drug-free society. Dignitaries and citizens present at the finale collectively reaffirmed their commitment by taking the Nasha Mukt Bharat Pledge. The concluding Sabha was also attended by former Governor of Maharashtra Shri C.H. Vidyasagar Rao, President of Ramakrishna Math Swami Bodhamayananda, renowned film director Shri Bandreddi Sukumar, Members of Parliament Shri Eatala Rajender and Shri Raghunandan Rao, and several other public representatives. Photo 13: Community members join in taking the Nasha Mukt Bharat pledge Photo 14: Citizens take the pledge at an evening gathering along the route Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar also joined the Padyatra. Former Governor Shri Bandaru Dattatreya and Member of Parliament Dr. K. Laxman participated in the campaign and took the Nasha Mukt Bharat Pledge with fellow participants. Members of Parliament Shri Eatala Rajender and Shri Konda Vishweshwar Reddy, MLA Shri Alleti Maheshwar Reddy, MLCs Dr. Chinnamail Anji Reddy and Shri Malka Komaraiah, among other elected representatives, also joined the walk at different points along the route. Several other legislators and public representatives, including MLAs Shri Katipally Venkata Ramana Reddy, Shri Ramarao Patil and Shri Dhanpal Suryanarayana, former MLC Shri N. Ramchander Rao and former MLA Shri Chintala Ramachandra Reddy, extended their support to the initiative. Photo 15: Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar joins the walk Photo 16: Padma Shri awardee Shri Gaddam Sammaiah joins the walk at the statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Photo 17: A young boy from the area joins the walk The Padyatra received notable support from eminent Padma awardees representing diverse fields of achievement. Padma Bhushan awardee Shri Pullela Gopichand, badminton legend and Chief National Coach of the Indian National Badminton Team, participated in the walk. Padma Shri awardees Smt. Deepika Reddy, renowned Kuchipudi exponent and choreographer; Shri Gaddam Sammaiah, eminent folk artist and exponent of Chindu Yakshagana; and Shri B.V.R. Mohan Reddy, Founder of Cyient Limited, also joined the campaign. The film fraternity extended enthusiastic support to the initiative. Popular actors Shri Akkineni Nagarjuna, Shri Daggubati Venkatesh, Shri Bellamkonda Sai Sreenivas, Shri Sai Kumar, Shri Nikhil Siddhartha and Kumari Payal Rajput participated in the walk. Photos 18 & 19: Padma Vibhushan awardee Dr. D. Nageshwar Reddy, former Governor of Maharashtra Shri C.H. Vidyasagar Rao, President of Ramakrishna Math Swami Bodhamayananda, renowned director Shri Bandreddi Sukumar, Former MLC  Shri N. Ramchander Rao, Hon’ble Members of Parliament Shri Eatala Rajender and Shri Raghunandan Rao, Hon’ble MLA Shri Alleti Maheshwar Reddy, Hon’ble MLAs Shri Katipally Venkata Ramana Reddy, Shri Ramarao Patil and Shri Dhanpal Suryanarayana, Hon’ble MLCs Dr. Chinnamail Anji Reddy and Shri Malka Komaraiah, and Former MLA Shri Chintala Ramachandra Reddy at the closing finale Renowned directors Shri Bandreddi Sukumar and Shri Boyapati Srinu, mimicry artist Shri Siva Reddy and television presenter and actress Smt. Suma Kanakala also extended their support. Shri Akkineni Nagarjuna appealed to citizens to become part of the collective movement for a drug-free India. Photo 20: Dignitaries take the Nasha Mukt Bharat pledge on stage at the closing finale, Jubilee Hills Photo 21: Felicitation with the ‘Hyderabad Walks for Nasha Mukt Bharat’ memento at the closing finale In the run-up to the Padyatra, Dr. K. Chiranjeevi, Shri Prabhas and Shri Akkineni Nagarjuna unveiled the campaign T-shirts along with Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy, while Directors Shri Bandreddi Sukumar and Shri Boyapati Srinu pledged their support to the initiative. Several prominent personalities extended their support virtually. These included pan-India film star Shri Prabhas, former Indian cricketer and Padma Shri awardee Shri V.V.S. Laxman, actress Kumari Kavya Kalyanram and Padma Shri awardee Dr. P. Vijay Anand Reddy, noted oncologist and Director of Apollo Cancer Centres. The academic community played an important role in the campaign, with Vice-Chancellors Prof. Kumar Molugaram of Osmania University, Prof. Y.L. Srinivas of Sammakka Sarakka Central Tribal University and Prof. N. Nagaraju of The English and Foreign Languages University (EFLU) joining the Padyatra along with faculty members and students. Photo 22: Addressing the gathering at the closing finale, Jubilee Hills - By Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar Photo 23: A message for a drug-free India from the closing finale stage - By Dr. K. Chiranjeevi The participation of universities and educational institutions reinforced the importance of engaging young people in preventive awareness, peer-led outreach and community-level action against substance abuse. Technology entrepreneurs, members of NGOs and other professionals also participated, demonstrating the broad-based support for the campaign. The successful culmination of the 40-kilometre Padyatra has reinforced the message that the fight against drug abuse cannot be left to government interventions alone. It requires active participation from every section of society, with particular emphasis on youth leadership, awareness, prevention, early intervention, counselling, rehabilitation and social reintegration. The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, seeks to create awareness about the harmful consequences of substance abuse and mobilize communities, particularly youth and vulnerable groups, towards a drug-free society.
